A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OccluGaussian work and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Retained content can be matched across appendix reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction, rendering-speed, clustering, and ablation results on OccluScene3D, Zip-NeRF, Mill-19, and UrbanScene3D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds Mip-NeRF 360 evaluations, six-scene OccluScene3D-E results, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The attributed view graph, cluster refinement, camera selection, region merging, visibility masks, and region-based rendering procedure remain unchanged. New configurations are experimental controls rather than proposed method changes.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluations on Garden and Kitchen from Mip-NeRF 360 and six additional OccluScene3D-E environments, including study, meeting, classroom, and parking scenes. This substantially broadens scene coverage and introduces small, relatively occlusion-free evaluation settings.

E2.justification: Figure 10 adds VastGaussian to the aerial scene-division visual comparison, which showed only OccluGaussian in v1. The existing quantitative comparator sets remain unchanged; vanilla 3DGS in the new Mip-NeRF 360 experiment is an already evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New controls include no-division versus two-block reconstruction, border-camera removal, and a Gallery sweep over K = 1, 5, 7, 10, 15. V2 also specifies 60k optimization steps and 200-step densification intervals for aerial experiments, versus v1's general 90k/100-step description. This changes the documented settings without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds border-camera ablation evidence in Figure 14, small-scene division controls in Table 10, and broader initialization sensitivity testing in Table 17. The revised Figure 10 also examines aerial scene shape and partitioning. Together these substantially extend component validation and applicability analysis beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial result entries in Tables 10, 16, and 17 and new qualitative evidence. Examples include Garden two-block PSNR of 27.37 and OccluScene3D-E scene PSNRs ranging from 22.24 to 27.00. These are newly reported evaluations, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, Laplacian, convolution, similarity construction in Equations 1–3, and visibility-mask formulation are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: occlusion-aware scene division improves reconstruction, and region-based culling accelerates rendering without noticeable quality loss. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains aerial-scene gains through more balanced camera allocation, with greater benefits for elongated than square scenes. It also discusses limited division benefits on small, low-occlusion scenes. The existing limitation concerning the initial cluster count remains unchanged.

D1.justification: New Section 6 discloses RTX 4090/V100 hardware, exclusion of preprocessing from training times, a 9.28-minute average division cost, and aerial block/downsampling details. Section 9 adds extended-dataset statistics and an access link. Conversely, v1's statement that 3% of video frames are uniformly extracted is removed.

R1.justification: The same 56 cited works and principal research positioning are retained. Numerous references receive venue, year, author-list, or other bibliographic updates, rather than representing added or removed research.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged, with limited grammatical and affiliation corrections. The supplement adds training-details and extended-dataset sections, expands several analysis paragraphs, and renumbers retained sections without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The supplement adds four tables and three figures covering small-scene controls, border-camera effects, extended-dataset statistics and renderings, and initialization sensitivity. Figure 10 becomes a paired aerial comparison, several existing figures receive graphical or labeling refinements, and appendix displays are substantially rearranged.

improvement.justification: Figure 14 now supports the border-camera rationale, while Table 10 tests when division helps; additional scenes broaden validation, and hardware/timing disclosures improve transparency. These strengthen the existing paper incrementally. The new six-scene results lack comparative baselines, while removal of the sampling fraction and differing general versus aerial training-budget descriptions limit the reproducibility gain.
